question: What is the best feeding item to use when giving ORS to an infant?

options.A: A clean cup and spoon
options.B: A rubber feeding bottle
options.C: A wide-spout drinking straw
options.D: A plastic syringe with a needle

explanation: Always choose a clean cup and spoon! Baby bottles have narrow parts that are very hard to clean properly and can easily trap germs that cause more infections. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h6)

question: For how long should a child take zinc supplements after having acute diarrhoea?

options.A: For at least six months
options.B: Only until the stool is firm
options.C: 10 to 14 days
options.D: 24 to 48 hours

explanation: Even if the child feels completely better after two days, completing the full 10 to 14 day course of zinc is vital to rebuild the gut lining and protect against future illness. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h7)

question: What is the main medical benefit of giving zinc supplements during childhood diarrhoea?

options.A: It instantly stops all vomiting within one hour
options.B: It replaces lost potassium in the bloodstream
options.C: It repairs the gut lining and shortens illness duration
options.D: It acts as a strong painkiller for stomach cramps

explanation: Zinc is wonderful for healing! It acts like medicine for the gut walls, helping them repair faster and boosting the child's immune system to clear the bug away. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h7)

question: Why is starting ORT right at home so important for community health?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any professional medical checkups
options.B: It prevents family members from catching the same stomach bug
options.C: It guarantees that the underlying viral infection will disappear overnight
options.D: It stops dehydration from progressing to a dangerous stage before reaching a clinic

explanation: Every minute counts! Giving fluids immediately at home stops mild fluid loss from turning into a life-threatening emergency before the family even reaches the hospital. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h8)

question: Which harmful traditional practice should nurses actively discourage when teaching mothers about diarrhoea?

options.A: Mixing ORS packets in clean drinking water
options.B: Withholding food and fluids to rest the bowel
options.C: Continuing to breastfeed the infant on demand
options.D: Giving zinc supplements for two full weeks

explanation: Never starve a tummy bug! Stopping food and water only makes malnutrition and dehydration worse. Children with diarrhoea need continued feeding and plenty of fluids to heal. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h8)

question: What was the traditional view of a man's primary role in family health?

options.A: Clinic scheduler
options.B: Primary caregiver
options.C: Financial provider
options.D: Health educator

explanation: Traditionally, men were viewed mainly as providers of money rather than active participants in daily health care and clinic visits. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h1)

question: Why is involving men in family health beneficial for the household?

options.A: It improves health outcomes for women and children
options.B: It reduces the household income requirement
options.C: It makes clinic visits shorter for everyone
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for nurses

explanation: Active male participation creates a supportive environment that directly boosts health and wellness for mothers and children. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h1)

question: Which socio-cultural factor most commonly discourages men from seeking early healthcare?

options.A: Lack of available male doctors
options.B: Strict government hospital regulations
options.C: Fear of paying high transport costs
options.D: Viewing health-seeking behavior as a sign of weakness

explanation: Traditional definitions of masculinity often make men hide illness or delay seeking help to appear strong. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h2)

question: What is the primary effect of patriarchal structures on family health responsibilities?

options.A: Men take on all nursing duties at home
options.B: Children become responsible for their own care
options.C: Health and domestic matters are left entirely to women
options.D: Couples share all medical decisions equally

explanation: Patriarchal norms often assign all caregiving and domestic duties to women, keeping men away from health spaces. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h2)

question: What is a major benefit of a man attending antenatal care visits with his partner?

options.A: He replaces the midwife during delivery
options.B: He can perform the physical examination himself
options.C: He learns about pregnancy danger signs and birth preparedness
options.D: He receives free medications for chronic illnesses

explanation: Attending antenatal visits helps fathers understand what complications to watch out for and how to prepare for emergencies. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h3)

question: A pregnant woman comes to the clinic with her husband who actively asks about emergency transport plans. How should the nurse view this behavior?

options.A: As a positive sign of male involvement in maternal health
options.B: As an unnecessary intrusion into clinical matters
options.C: As proof that the woman cannot care for herself
options.D: As a violation of hospital privacy policies

explanation: Planning for emergency transport with a partner shows strong male involvement which protects maternal and newborn health. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h3)

question: Why is male involvement important in family planning decisions?

options.A: It reduces the cost of buying medications
options.B: It gives men total control over family size
options.C: It removes the need for female contraceptive use
options.D: It ensures joint agreement and supports birth spacing

explanation: Family planning works best when both partners discuss and agree on methods that protect the health of the mother. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h4)

question: What is a common misconception regarding family planning services in many communities?

options.A: It is only meant for couples with no children
options.B: It is exclusively a female responsibility
options.C: It is completely free at all hospitals
options.D: It is dangerous for men to discuss it

explanation: Many people incorrectly believe that contraception and birth spacing concern only women, leaving men out of the conversation. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier keeping men away from health clinics?

options.A: Staff attitudes that treat men as unwelcome intruders
options.B: Clinics operating convenient evening and weekend hours
options.C: Long waiting times that clash with work schedules
options.D: Facility environments focused solely on mothers and babies

explanation: Convenient operating hours would actually encourage attendance, whereas the other options represent real barriers men face. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h5)

question: Why do daily wage earners find it difficult to attend primary healthcare clinics during the day?

options.A: Clinics refuse to treat people who work in the informal sector
options.B: Transportation is completely unavailable during daytime hours
options.C: Doctors only consult patients during the night
options.D: They lose a day of critical income while waiting at the hospital

explanation: Long daytime waiting hours present a direct financial penalty for men who depend on daily wages to survive. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h5)

question: How do male champions help improve men's participation in family health?

options.A: By setting a positive example and discussing health openly among peers
options.B: By paying all the medical bills for families in the community
options.C: By taking over the duties of healthcare providers at the clinic
options.D: By forcing other men to visit hospitals through legal action

explanation: Respected peers break down cultural barriers by openly sharing their own positive experiences with clinic attendance. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h6)

question: A primary health center wants to attract more working fathers to clinics. Which strategy is most effective?

options.A: Stopping all maternal health services to focus only on men
options.B: Introducing flexible clinic hours or dedicated men's health desks
options.C: Banning women from entering the clinic alone
options.D: Punishing men who refuse to attend antenatal visits

explanation: Creating welcoming spaces and flexible schedules accommodates men's work realities and encourages them to participate. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h6)

question: What is a key action Nigerian nurses can take to promote male involvement?

options.A: Send police officers to bring absent fathers to the hospital
options.B: Ignore fathers in the waiting room to focus only on mothers
options.C: Actively invite men into consultation rooms and address both parents
options.D: Charge men extra fees for entering maternal health clinics

explanation: Nurses promote involvement by making fathers feel welcome and included in health discussions right from the start. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h7)

question: Why must nurses work to eliminate personal bias regarding gender roles in the clinic?

options.A: Hospital management requires all nurses to pass a gender exam
options.B: Biases prevent nurses from dispensing medications properly
options.C: Ministry of health guidelines ban nurses from talking to men
options.D: Biased attitudes can make men feel unwelcome and drive them away from care

explanation: When nurses act judgmentally or ignore fathers, it reinforces the belief that health clinics are not meant for men. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h7)

question: What is the primary meaning of women empowerment in a healthcare context?

options.A: Gaining control and the ability to make choices about health and life
options.B: Eliminating the need for medical practitioners in rural villages
options.C: Taking over leadership roles exclusively in hospital management boards
options.D: Ensuring women work exclusively outside the home environment

explanation: Empowerment centers on gaining personal autonomy and the capacity to make vital decisions regarding one's health and well-being. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T59#GNS214_U1_T59_h1)

question: Why is women empowerment considered essential for achieving universal health coverage?

options.A: It stops the government from building more primary health centers
options.B: It allows women to actively participate in seeking and utilizing healthcare services
options.C: It completely removes the financial cost of purchasing hospital drugs
options.D: It guarantees that only female doctors will treat patients

explanation: When women have autonomy, they can freely access health facilities and make prompt decisions that improve community health indices. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T59#GNS214_U1_T59_h1)

question: What is a major economic barrier that limits a woman's healthcare autonomy?

options.A: Financial dependency on male heads of households
options.B: Too much freedom in spending personal income
options.C: An overabundance of free public health clinics
options.D: Excessive participation in local market associations

explanation: Without personal income or financial control, women often cannot afford transport fare or medical bills without male approval. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T59#GNS214_U1_T59_h2)

question: How does formal education directly improve a woman's health decision-making?

options.A: It forces community leaders to consult her on political matters
options.B: It automatically exempts her family from paying hospital taxes
options.C: It increases her financial literacy, self-confidence, and health awareness
options.D: It legally prevents her from visiting traditional birth attendants

explanation: Educated women generally possess better literacy skills to understand health instructions and have more confidence to seek prompt medical care. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T59#GNS214_U1_T59_h2)

question: Which factor contributes most directly to delays in treating obstetric emergencies?

options.A: Needing permission from family members before seeking care
options.B: Excessive availability of ambulance services in rural areas
options.C: Early registration for routine antenatal care
options.D: Having too many nurses on duty at the primary health center

explanation: When a woman lacks decision-making power, waiting for authorization from male or elderly relatives causes dangerous delays during emergencies. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T59#GNS214_U1_T59_h3)

question: A pregnant woman in labor notices severe vaginal bleeding but refuses to go to the hospital until her husband returns from a distant trip. What concept does this situation highlight?

options.A: Superior financial planning for hospital delivery costs
options.B: Effective community-based healthcare mobilization
options.C: Lack of maternal autonomy and delayed emergency decision-making
options.D: Excellent adherence to cultural birth preparation guidelines

explanation: Waiting for absent approval during a life-threatening crisis demonstrates a dangerous absence of personal health autonomy. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T59#GNS214_U1_T59_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common social barrier to women empowerment in local communities?

options.A: Universal free access to university education for all females
options.B: Religious misinterpretations regarding modern healthcare use
options.C: Patriarchal norms that demand absolute female submission
options.D: Fear of domestic violence or social punishment

explanation: Universal free education is a facilitator of empowerment, not a barrier; the other options represent actual obstacles women face. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T59#GNS214_U1_T59_h4)

question: Why do patriarchal community norms negatively affect child health outcomes?

options.A: They restrict mothers from making independent medical choices for sick children
options.B: They encourage mothers to lead community health committees
options.C: They force fathers to spend all their income on infant vaccines
options.D: They automatically increase the nutritional value of local foods

explanation: When mothers lack household authority, they cannot easily take a sick child to the clinic without prior approval from male heads. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T59#GNS214_U1_T59_h4)

question: What is an effective community strategy for improving female financial independence?

options.A: Discouraging women from learning vocational skills
options.B: Requiring men to manage all household savings accounts
options.C: Forming local women cooperatives and financial support groups
options.D: Banning women from participating in traditional market trading

explanation: Cooperatives allow women to save money together, build small businesses, and gain financial freedom. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T59#GNS214_U1_T59_h5)

question: A community health nurse wants to introduce family planning in a conservative village where husbands oppose it. What is the best initial step?

options.A: Provide confidential medications to women without telling their families
options.B: Report uncooperative husbands to the local police station immediately
options.C: Stop all health outreaches until the villagers change their minds
options.D: Engage male community leaders and husbands in open health education discussions

explanation: Involving male champions helps reduce resistance and builds community-wide acceptance of health initiatives. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T59#GNS214_U1_T59_h5)

question: Up to how many days after a pregnancy ends is a death still officially counted as maternal mortality?

options.A: Within 1 year
options.B: Within 6 months
options.C: Within 7 days
options.D: Within 42 days

explanation: You've got this! A maternal death is counted if it happens during pregnancy or up to 42 days (6 weeks) after delivery from pregnancy-related causes. Keep up the great revision! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h1)

question: As a nursing student, how should you easily tell the difference between 'morbidity' and 'mortality'?

options.A: Morbidity is a statistic while mortality is a clinical diagnosis
options.B: Morbidity refers to illness while mortality refers to death
options.C: Morbidity affects only infants while mortality affects mothers
options.D: Morbidity is always preventable while mortality is inevitable

explanation: Think of it this way: morbidity means being sick or having health complications, while mortality simply means death. Simple and clear! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h1)

question: When public health experts calculate the Maternal Mortality Ratio, what is the standard denominator used?

options.A: Per 10,000 total women
options.B: Per 100,000 live births
options.C: Per 1,000 live births
options.D: Per 1,000 pregnant women

explanation: Great to know for exams and clinical practice: maternal mortality ratio is always expressed per 100,000 live births. You're doing brilliantly! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h2)

question: Why do we often see higher maternal and child mortality rates in rural Nigerian communities compared to big cities?

options.A: Rural populations have a higher birth rate per family
options.B: Rural residents completely reject modern medicine due to cultural laws
options.C: Urban populations have stronger immune systems from birth
options.D: Rural areas have limited access to equipped health facilities and skilled birth attendants

explanation: Spot on! Bad roads, long distances, and lack of well-equipped clinics mean emergencies take too long to reach help. This is why community health nursing is so vital in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h2)

question: What is the number one direct cause of maternal death all over the world?

options.A: Gestational diabetes
options.B: Severe dehydration
options.C: Hyperemesis gravidarum
options.D: Postpartum hemorrhage

explanation: Severe bleeding after childbirth (PPH) is the leading global killer of new mothers. As a nurse, knowing how to spot and manage PPH can literally save a life! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h3)

question: A newborn baby fails to cry or breathe right after delivery. What do we call this emergency?

options.A: Birth asphyxia
options.B: Neonatal jaundice
options.C: Congenital anomaly
options.D: Infant malnutrition

explanation: When a baby can't breathe on their own at birth, it's called birth asphyxia. Quick resuscitation is the key here—you'll practice this a lot in your midwifery postings! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h3)

question: What is the main reason midwives and nurses use a partograph during labor?

options.A: To record the baby's immunization schedule after birth
options.B: To calculate the exact date of conception for the mother
options.C: To monitor the progress of labor and detect complications early
options.D: To measure the exact blood volume lost during delivery

explanation: The partograph is your best friend in the labor ward! It gives a clear picture of how labor is advancing so you can catch trouble early before it harms mum or baby. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h4)

question: Why must nurses watch a mother and newborn extra closely immediately after delivery?

options.A: A high proportion of maternal and newborn deaths happen within the first 48 hours
options.B: The mother is usually discharged home immediately without any risk
options.C: Hormonal changes stop completely after the placenta is delivered
options.D: Newborns do not require feeding assistance until day three of life

explanation: The first 48 hours are the riskiest time for sudden bleeding, infections, or newborn collapse. Close monitoring keeps both mum and baby safe! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h4)

question: Which injection is routinely given to every newborn baby to prevent dangerous bleeding?

options.A: Vitamin K
options.B: Iron drops
options.C: Vitamin C
options.D: Folic acid

explanation: Newborns have little tummies that haven't built up clotting factors yet. Giving Vitamin K right after birth protects them against bleeding disorders. Excellent clinical knowledge to carry into the ward! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h5)

question: What is the wonderful benefit of placing a newborn baby skin-to-skin on the mother's chest right after birth?

options.A: It helps maintain the baby's body temperature and promotes early breastfeeding
options.B: It replaces the need for routine childhood immunizations
options.C: It completely eliminates the risk of neonatal jaundice
options.D: It speeds up the delivery of the remaining placenta

explanation: Skin-to-skin contact is magical! It keeps the baby warm, stabilizes their heart rate, and helps them find the breast easily. Nature at its finest! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h5)

question: What is the recommended minimum time a mother should wait before getting pregnant again, to protect her health and her child's?

options.A: Five years
options.B: One year
options.C: Six months
options.D: Two to three years

explanation: Giving at least 2 to 3 years between pregnancies lets the mother's body recover, rebuild her nutrient stores, and give the next baby a healthy start. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h6)

question: How does poor nutrition in a pregnant mother directly affect her unborn baby?

options.A: It prevents the development of neonatal jaundice entirely
options.B: It causes the baby to be born with complete immunity to infections
options.C: It accelerates the closure of the infant's fontanelles
options.D: It increases the risk of low birth weight and developmental stunting

explanation: A baby's growth depends totally on what the mother eats. Poor maternal nutrition often leads to low birth weight babies who have a harder time fighting off sickness. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h6)

question: Why are functional emergency referral systems so important for pregnant women in rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: Government policy requires all babies to be born in teaching hospitals
options.B: Patients prefer to pay higher fees at tertiary hospitals rather than local clinics
options.C: Primary health clinics cannot manage severe obstetric emergencies like ruptured uterus or eclampsia
options.D: Primary health centers do not keep any medical records of pregnant women

explanation: Local clinics are great for routine antenatal care, but if a life-threatening emergency like severe eclampsia happens, patients need quick transport to a bigger hospital with a doctor and blood bank. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h7)

question: Which of these options is NOT a helpful way to run a community-based healthcare strategy?

options.A: Educating local leaders on recognizing pregnancy danger signs
options.B: Mobilizing women for local immunization campaigns
options.C: Relying solely on tertiary hospitals without community outreach
options.D: Creating community emergency transport networks

explanation: Good healthcare goes to the people! Waiting in a big teaching hospital and ignoring local grassroots outreach leaves rural mothers helpless. You're smashing these questions! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h7)

question: What is the main public health goal of achieving high herd immunity within a community?

options.A: To guarantee lifelong immunity without booster doses
options.B: To protect vulnerable individuals who cannot receive vaccines
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of hospital admissions
options.D: To completely eliminate all known chronic illnesses

explanation: When most of the population is vaccinated, it creates a protective barrier that stops infectious agents from reaching people who are too young or sick to get vaccinated. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h1)

question: Why is immunization considered a fundamental component of Primary Health Care?

options.A: It is delivered exclusively inside major tertiary teaching hospitals
options.B: It replaces the need for proper sanitation and clean drinking water
options.C: It provides affordable, community-based disease prevention for all
options.D: It focuses on treating advanced stages of communicable diseases

explanation: Primary Health Care aims to bring essential health services as close as possible to where people live, making preventive measures like vaccines easily accessible. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h1)

question: How does an infant acquire natural passive immunity from their mother?

options.A: Through receiving routine childhood routine immunizations
options.B: By producing antibodies after surviving a childhood illness
options.C: By inheriting active immune memory cells during conception
options.D: Through the transfer of maternal antibodies via breast milk

explanation: Maternal antibodies pass to the baby across the placenta and through breast milk, giving the newborn temporary protection against common infections. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h2)

question: What is the primary clinical advantage of active immunity over passive immunity?

options.A: Active immunity does not require exposure to any antigens
options.B: Active immunity can be easily transferred through blood transfusions
options.C: Active immunity lasts much longer due to immunological memory
options.D: Active immunity provides immediate protection within minutes

explanation: When the body creates its own antibodies and memory cells during active immunity, it remembers the germ and protects against future exposures for years. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h2)

question: Which vaccines are routinely scheduled to be given immediately at birth in Nigeria?

options.A: BCG, OPV zero, and Hepatitis B zero
options.B: Pentavalent first dose and Rotavirus vaccine
options.C: Measles, Yellow fever, and Meningitis vaccines
options.D: Inactivated Polio Vaccine and PCV first dose

explanation: At birth, newborns receive BCG for tuberculosis, OPV 0 for polio, and the birth dose of Hepatitis B to prevent early mother-to-child transmission. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h3)

question: A mother brings her healthy 14-week-old infant to the primary health clinic. Which group of vaccines is due for this visit?

options.A: BCG, OPV zero, and Hepatitis B birth dose
options.B: Measles first dose and Yellow Fever vaccine
options.C: Rotavirus first dose and Pentavalent first dose
options.D: Pentavalent third dose, OPV 3, IPV, and PCV 3

explanation: At 14 weeks, infants receive the third doses of Pentavalent, OPV, and PCV, along with the first dose of Inactivated Polio Vaccine (IPV). [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h3)

question: What is the primary clinical complication caused by the poliovirus?

options.A: Irreversible muscle paralysis in the limbs
options.B: High fever accompanied by a widespread skin rash
options.C: Uncontrollable fits of violent coughing
options.D: Severe chronic diarrhea and rapid dehydration

explanation: Poliovirus attacks the nervous system, which can lead to total, permanent paralysis, most commonly affecting the legs. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h4)

question: Which of the following describes the main characteristic feature of pertussis infection?

options.A: Persistent watery diarrhea lasting several weeks
options.B: Violent and uncontrollable coughing spells
options.C: Yellow discoloration of the skin and eyes
options.D: Stiff jaw muscles and painful body spasms

explanation: Pertussis, commonly known as whooping cough, is famous for causing severe, hacking cough fits that end with a high-pitched whooping sound. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h4)

question: What is the safe temperature range for storing routine vaccines like Pentavalent and PCV in a clinic refrigerator?

options.B: +2°C to +8°C

explanation: Routine diluents and liquid vaccines like Pentavalent and PCV must be kept cool between two and eight degrees Celsius and never frozen. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of a Vaccine Vial Monitor (VVM) attached to a vaccine container?

options.A: To indicate if the vaccine has been exposed to damaging heat
options.B: To detect if the vaccine has accidentally been frozen solid
options.C: To measure the exact expiry date set by the factory
options.D: To show the precise number of vaccine doses remaining inside

explanation: The VVM changes color progressively when exposed to heat over time, giving nurses a visual warning that the vaccine potency may be compromised. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h5)

question: Which injection route is standard for administering the Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccine to a newborn?

options.A: Deep intravenous bolus injection into a peripheral vein
options.B: Intramuscular injection into the thigh muscle
options.C: Intradermal injection to create a shallow skin wheal
options.D: Subcutaneous injection into the fatty arm tissue

explanation: BCG is given intradermally into the superficial layers of the skin, typically on the upper arm, producing a characteristic small raised bleb. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h6)

question: Why are auto-disable syringes specifically used during routine immunization campaigns?

options.A: They lock automatically after one use to prevent accidental reuse
options.B: They allow nurses to draw medication much faster than regular needles
options.C: They can be safely disposed of in regular household waste bins
options.D: They reduce the physical pain of the injection for crying infants

explanation: Auto-disable syringes are designed to render themselves unserviceable after a single injection, stopping the spread of infections from reused equipment. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h6)

question: What is the immediate drug of choice for managing severe anaphylactic shock following a vaccination?

options.A: Oral paracetamol syrup
options.B: Intravenous normal saline
options.C: Subcutaneous hydrocortisone
options.D: Intramuscular epinephrine

explanation: Epinephrine is the life-saving treatment for anaphylaxis because it quickly constricts blood vessels, relaxes airway passages, and raises dropping blood pressure. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h7)

question: Which event is classified as an immunization error-related adverse event?

options.A: A child developing a mild fever due to an immune response
options.B: A mild allergic rash caused by an egg protein allergy
options.C: An abscess forming due to unsterile injection techniques
options.D: A baby catching an unrelated malaria infection the next day

explanation: Immunization errors happen due to mistakes in handling, preparation, or administration, such as introducing bacteria through poor aseptic technique. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h7)

question: How should a nurse best approach a caregiver who expresses fear and hesitation about routine childhood vaccines?

options.A: Scold the parent for ignoring professional medical advice
options.B: Report the parent to local law enforcement authorities
options.C: Listen respectfully and provide clear, reassuring education
options.D: Ignore their concerns and administer the vaccines anyway

explanation: Building trust through empathetic listening and clear, respectful communication is the most effective way to address vaccine hesitancy and correct rumors. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h8)

question: What is the most effective way to improve community participation in rural immunization drives?

options.A: Relying solely on written posters placed inside clinic walls
options.B: Stopping all routine clinic visits to focus only on mass rallies
options.C: Engaging local community and religious leaders as advocates
options.D: Punishing parents who fail to bring their babies on time

explanation: Working with respected community and religious leaders helps build local trust and encourages families to accept and support immunization programs. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h8)

question: How do vaccines protect the human body against specific diseases?

options.A: Destroying all bacteria currently living in the gut
options.B: Increasing the overall body temperature to kill viruses
options.C: Stimulating antibody production without causing illness
options.D: Providing permanent chemical antibiotics in the blood

explanation: Spot on! Vaccines introduce harmless pieces or weakened parts of a germ so your immune system can safely learn to fight it without getting you sick. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T62#GNS214_U1_T62_h1)

question: Why is herd immunity so important for infants who are too young for certain vaccines?

options.A: It cures any congenital infections the infant was born with
options.B: It lowers the chance that the infant will encounter the infectious agent
options.C: It passes mature white blood cells directly through breast milk
options.D: It permanently removes all pathogens from the surrounding environment

explanation: You got it! When everyone around the baby is vaccinated, it builds a protective shield that keeps nasty germs far away from vulnerable little ones. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T62#GNS214_U1_T62_h1)

question: Which two vaccines are routinely given to newborns right at birth in Nigeria?

options.A: BCG and Oral Polio Vaccine zero
options.B: Pentavalent and Tetanus toxoid
options.C: Hepatitis A and Rabies vaccine
options.D: Measles and Yellow Fever vaccine

explanation: Exactly! Right after delivery, babies receive the BCG shot against tuberculosis and their first drops of oral polio vaccine (OPV 0). [learn more](GNS214_U1_T62#GNS214_U1_T62_h2)

question: An infant is brought in at exactly 14 weeks for routine immunization. Which vaccines should you expect to give?

options.A: Final infant doses of polio, pentavalent, and pneumococcal
options.B: Yellow fever and initial oral polio vaccine zero
options.C: BCG and first dose of measles
options.D: Only the annual influenza booster shot

explanation: Well done! At 14 weeks, babies complete their final scheduled series of OPV, IPV, pentavalent, and pneumococcal vaccines. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T62#GNS214_U1_T62_h2)

question: How is the BCG vaccine usually given to a newborn?

options.A: Subcutaneously in the thigh
options.B: Intradermally into the skin
options.C: Orally using liquid drops
options.D: Deep intramuscular injection

explanation: Correct! BCG goes just under the top layer of skin (intradermally), usually on the upper left arm, leaving a small bump that later turns into a scar. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T62#GNS214_U1_T62_h3)

question: What is the main way the poliovirus spreads in a community?

options.A: Inhalation of respiratory droplets from sneezing
options.B: Direct skin contact with an infected skin rash
options.C: Vector-borne transmission via mosquito bites
options.D: Fecal-oral route through contaminated water or food

explanation: Spot on! Polio spreads mainly through the fecal-oral route, usually when people consume food or water contaminated with infected waste. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T62#GNS214_U1_T62_h3)

question: Which sign is a classic clue that a patient has a respiratory diphtheria infection?

options.A: Uncontrollable whooping sounds during inhalation
options.B: A fluid-filled rash covering the entire trunk
options.C: A thick grey membrane obstructing the throat
options.D: Severe painful muscle spasms and body arching

explanation: You nailed it! Diphtheria forms a tough, greyish membrane in the throat that can dangerousy block airflow and release toxins. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T62#GNS214_U1_T62_h4)

question: What is the main cause of neonatal tetanus in newborn babies?

options.A: Mother-to-child transmission across the placenta during birth
options.B: Unhygienic practices during umbilical cord cutting and care
options.C: Inhalation of airborne bacterial droplets from coughing adults
options.D: Consuming unpasteurized milk during the first week of life

explanation: Correct! Neonatal tetanus happens when tetanus germs get into the unhealed umbilical stump, often due to unsterilized instruments. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T62#GNS214_U1_T62_h4)

question: Which clinical finding shows up early in a measles infection?

options.A: Yellow discoloration of the eye sclera
options.B: Painful spasms of the jaw muscles
options.C: Koplik spots inside the oral cavity
options.D: A thick grey membrane in the throat

explanation: Spot on! Koplik spots look like tiny grains of salt on a red background inside the cheeks, and they are a dead giveaway for early measles. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T62#GNS214_U1_T62_h5)

question: Why should a newborn get their first Hepatitis B vaccine within 24 hours of birth?

options.A: To protect against mosquito bites acquired outdoors
options.B: To prevent severe dehydration caused by watery diarrhea
options.C: To prevent mother-to-child transmission of the virus
options.D: To stop bacterial growth in the umbilical cord stump

explanation: You got it! Giving this dose immediately blocks the virus from passing from an infected mother to her baby during delivery. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T62#GNS214_U1_T62_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a common symptom of meningococcal meningitis?

options.A: Severe headache
options.B: Sudden high fever
options.C: Stiff neck
options.D: Persistent watery diarrhea

explanation: Correct! Meningitis attacks the brain and spinal cord lining (causing fever, headache, and stiff neck), while watery diarrhea points to a gut infection instead. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T62#GNS214_U1_T62_h6)

question: How does the Hib part of the pentavalent vaccine help protect young children?

options.A: By stopping spasms caused by tetanus spores in the umbilical cord
options.B: By stopping the production of abnormal liver enzymes in blood
options.C: By preventing severe respiratory infections and bacterial meningitis
options.D: By blocking the transmission of the yellow fever mosquito vector

explanation: Well done! Hib (Haemophilus influenzae type b) is a nasty bacteria that causes severe pneumonia and meningitis, which this vaccine successfully stops. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T62#GNS214_U1_T62_h6)

question: What is the main reason for keeping vaccines in the cold chain?

options.A: To prevent the growth of beneficial bacteria inside vials
options.B: To preserve the chemical potency of the vaccine
options.C: To make the liquid easier to draw into a syringe
options.D: To freeze the vaccine solid before giving it to a child

explanation: Spot on! Vaccines are delicate biological products. The cold chain ensures they don't spoil and lose their disease-fighting power. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T62#GNS214_U1_T62_h7)

question: What goes wrong when vaccines like the pentavalent injection get accidentally frozen?

options.A: The formation of harmless sugar crystals that dissolve
options.B: An increase in the shelf life past the expiry date
options.C: Permanent damage to the vaccine's potency
options.D: A change in the color of the liquid to bright yellow

explanation: Correct! Freezing ruins vaccines that contain aluminum adjuvants (like pentavalent), completely destroying their effectiveness. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T62#GNS214_U1_T62_h7)

question: What is the best way for a nurse to handle vaccine hesitancy from a caregiver?

options.A: Telling the caregiver that their personal beliefs are completely wrong
options.B: Listening respectfully to concerns and providing clear facts
options.C: Threatening to withhold other basic primary healthcare services
options.D: Ignoring the questions and quickly administering the injection anyway

explanation: You nailed it! Building trust through patience, empathy, and gentle education works way better than arguing or judging. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T62#GNS214_U1_T62_h8)

question: A mother is worried because her baby had a mild fever and swelling after their last shot. How should you respond?

options.A: Advise the mother never to bring the child back for any future immunizations
options.B: Report the child to public health authorities for failing a routine check
options.C: Explain that these mild reactions are normal signs of the immune system working
options.D: Immediately prescribe strong oral antibiotics to treat an expected infection

explanation: Spot on! A little soreness or low-grade fever just means the baby's immune system is busy building up its defenses. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T62#GNS214_U1_T62_h8)

question: What is the main goal of Universal Child Immunization?

options.A: Treating chronic illnesses in school-aged children
options.B: Eliminating all known bacterial infections globally
options.C: Providing nutritional supplements to newborns
options.D: Ensuring every infant receives essential vaccines before one year of age

explanation: You got this! Universal Child Immunization focuses on getting babies protected against dangerous, preventable diseases during their very first year of life. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T63#GNS214_U1_T63_h1)

question: Why is herd immunity so helpful for babies in a community?

options.A: It protects babies who are too young to be vaccinated themselves
options.B: It removes the need for cold chain storage in local clinics
options.C: It cures children who already have a vaccine-preventable disease
options.D: It guarantees that mothers produce more antibodies in breast milk

explanation: Spot on! When most people around them are immunized, it creates a protective shield that stops germs from reaching vulnerable infants. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T63#GNS214_U1_T63_h1)

question: Which vaccines does a newborn baby routinely receive right at birth here in Nigeria?

options.A: Measles and Yellow Fever
options.B: Pentavalent and Rotavirus
options.C: Tetanus and Hepatitis A
options.D: BCG and Oral Polio Vaccine

explanation: Great job! Right after birth, babies get BCG to fight tuberculosis and the first dose (zero dose) of oral polio vaccine. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T63#GNS214_U1_T63_h2)

question: At what age does a baby get their first dose of the measles vaccine?

options.A: At 9 months of age
options.B: At birth
options.C: At 6 weeks of age
options.D: At 14 weeks of age

explanation: Exactly! We wait until 9 months because antibodies passed down from the mother can block the measles vaccine if given too early. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T63#GNS214_U1_T63_h2)

question: What is the safe temperature range for storing most routine vaccines in a clinic fridge?

options.A: Between +2°C and +8°C
options.B: Between -10°C and -20°C
options.C: Between +30°C and +40°C
options.D: Between +15°C and +25°C

explanation: You nailed it! Keeping the fridge between +2°C and +8°C keeps vaccines safe without letting them freeze or overheat. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T63#GNS214_U1_T63_h3)

question: A nurse is packing a vaccine carrier for an outreach. What must be avoided to protect the vaccines?

options.A: Keeping the lid of the vaccine carrier tightly closed between uses
options.B: Placing frozen ice packs directly touching liquid vaccines
options.C: Lining the bottom of the vaccine carrier with conditioned ice packs
options.D: Checking the temperature of the cold box using a stem thermometer

explanation: Spot on! Direct contact with freezing ice can ruin liquid vaccines like pentavalent by freezing them solid. Always use conditioned ice packs! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T63#GNS214_U1_T63_h3)

question: Which of these is a TRUE reason to skip or stop a routine childhood vaccine?

options.A: A severe allergic reaction after a previous dose of the same vaccine
options.B: Low-grade fever and mild watery diarrhea
options.C: A mild upper respiratory tract infection with a runny nose
options.D: A family history of minor skin rashes after medication

explanation: Well done! A severe reaction (like anaphylaxis) to a prior dose means we must not give that specific vaccine again. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T63#GNS214_U1_T63_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a valid reason to delay vaccinating a sick child?

options.A: Having known severe immunodeficiency for live vaccines
options.B: Experiencing a severe anaphylactic reaction to the previous injection
options.C: Having a mild cough and low-grade fever
options.D: Showing signs of active encephalopathy after a pertussis shot

explanation: Exactly! Minor coughs or low fevers won't stop the baby's immune system from responding, so don't miss the chance to vaccinate them. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T63#GNS214_U1_T63_h4)

question: Where is the best place on an infant's body to give an intramuscular (IM) injection?

options.A: Inner aspect of the forearm
options.B: Deltoid muscle of the upper arm
options.C: Anterolateral aspect of the thigh
options.D: Upper outer quadrant of the buttocks

explanation: You got it! The thigh muscle is safe and large in babies, and it keeps us safely away from the sciatic nerve in the buttocks. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T63#GNS214_U1_T63_h5)

question: At what angle should a nurse insert the needle for a subcutaneous vaccine like measles?

options.A: At a 90-degree angle
options.B: At a 45-degree angle
options.C: At a 15-degree angle
options.D: Straight down at a 180-degree angle

explanation: Spot on! A 45-degree angle lets you place the vaccine nicely into the fatty layer just under the skin instead of going deep into the muscle. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T63#GNS214_U1_T63_h5)

question: What is a normal, mild reaction parents can expect after their baby's immunizations?

options.A: Sudden onset of severe jaundice
options.B: Slight soreness and redness at the injection site
options.C: Generalized body paralysis within two hours
options.D: Permanent hearing loss in both ears

explanation: Great work! Mild swelling or soreness is just a normal sign that the baby's body is building immunity, and it goes away on its own. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T63#GNS214_U1_T63_h6)

question: Why must clinic nurses report unusual or severe side effects (AEFIs) to health authorities?

options.A: To punish the community health worker who administered the injection
options.B: To stop mothers from bringing their babies for future visits
options.C: To investigate vaccine safety and maintain public trust in the program
options.D: To immediately ban all vaccine manufacturing in the country

explanation: Exactly right! Reporting helps health teams track safety, catch batch issues early, and keep parents confident in immunizations. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T63#GNS214_U1_T63_h6)

question: How should a nurse respond to a mother who is worried and hesitant about vaccines?

options.A: Tell her that asking questions about health is illegal and disrespectful
options.B: Listen patiently, address her specific worries with facts, and show empathy
options.C: Scold her for neglecting her child and refuse to serve her today
options.D: Ignore her concerns and quickly give the injections without talking

explanation: You've got this! Warm listening and gentle, fact-based guidance are the best ways to ease a parent's worries and build trust. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T63#GNS214_U1_T63_h7)

question: What is a great way to improve vaccine turnout in a hesitant rural community?

options.A: Stopping all outreach visits and waiting for parents to find the clinic
options.B: Collaborating with respected local leaders and traditional rulers for health talks
options.C: Threatening parents with police arrest if they miss clinic appointments
options.D: Hiding the vaccine vials so people do not know what is being injected

explanation: Spot on! Traditional and community leaders have great influence and can help clear up rumors so families feel safe bringing their children. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T63#GNS214_U1_T63_h7)

question: Where should a nurse record every vaccine dose right after giving it to a baby?

options.A: Inside the national census database via text message only
options.B: Only in the nurse's personal notebook at home
options.C: In the child's home-based health card and the facility register
options.D: On a scrap piece of paper to be discarded at the end of the day

explanation: Great job! Writing it in both the child's card and the clinic book ensures good record-keeping and smooth follow-up care. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T63#GNS214_U1_T63_h8)

question: What is the main problem when a mother loses her child's immunization card?

options.A: An automatic fine issued by the local health department
options.B: Immediate development of vaccine-preventable diseases in the infant
options.C: The child losing all previous immunity built by past doses
options.D: Difficulty knowing which future vaccines the child needs and when

explanation: Exactly! Without the card, it's hard to tell for sure which doses the baby has already received and when the next one is due. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T63#GNS214_U1_T63_h8)

question: What is the primary target group for routine immunization under the NPI in Nigeria?

options.A: Infants and pregnant women
options.B: Elderly patients with chronic illness
options.C: Adolescents in secondary schools
options.D: Adult males in urban centers

explanation: The NPI primarily focuses on protecting vulnerable groups like infants and pregnant women from vaccine-preventable infections. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h1)

question: Why is integrating the NPI into Primary Health Care essential for rural communities?

options.A: It brings life-saving vaccines closer to grassroots populations
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for vaccine cold storage
options.C: It allows traditional birth attendants to manufacture vaccines
options.D: It replaces the need for community health extension workers

explanation: Primary Health Care integration ensures that rural and hard-to-reach populations have physical access to immunization services. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h1)

question: A major objective of the NPI in Nigeria is the elimination of which specific disease?

options.A: Sickle cell crisis
options.B: Adult-onset diabetes
options.C: Maternal and neonatal tetanus
options.D: Hypertension in pregnancy

explanation: Eliminating maternal and neonatal tetanus through routine immunization and clean delivery practices remains a primary objective of the program. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h2)

question: Community participation in the NPI is important because it achieves what outcome?

options.A: Eliminates the requirement for cold chain maintenance
options.B: Builds local ownership and increases vaccine acceptance
options.C: Provides financial funding for vaccine manufacturing
options.D: Reduces the workload of trained nursing personnel

explanation: Involving community leaders and members fosters trust and encourages mothers to complete their children's immunization schedules. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h2)

question: Which vaccine is routinely given to a newborn baby immediately at birth in Nigeria?

options.A: Pentavalent and booster doses
options.B: Measles and yellow fever vaccine
options.C: BCG and zero dose OPV
options.D: Tetanus toxoid and PCV

explanation: Newborns receive BCG for tuberculosis protection and the zero dose of Oral Polio Vaccine right at birth. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h3)

question: A mother brings her 14-week-old infant to the clinic. Which combination of vaccines is due at this visit?

options.A: Third doses of Pentavalent, PCV, and OPV
options.B: BCG and first dose of measles vaccine
options.C: Yellow fever and adult tetanus toxoid
options.D: Only the birth dose of polio vaccine

explanation: The routine schedule dictates that the third contact at 14 weeks includes the third doses of Pentavalent, PCV, and OPV. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h3)

question: What is the recommended safe storage temperature range for most routine refrigerated vaccines?

options.A: +2°C to +8°C

explanation: Most routine vaccines must be kept in standard refrigerators operating strictly between +2°C and +8°C to maintain potency. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h4)

question: What happens to toxoid vaccines like Pentavalent if they are accidentally frozen?

options.A: Their expiration date is automatically extended
options.B: They lose their potency and become ineffective
options.C: They change color to indicate safe usage
options.D: They become safer and stronger for the infant

explanation: Freezing causes toxoid vaccines to clump and lose their immunological potency, making them useless for protection. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h4)

question: What is the correct anatomical site for giving intramuscular routine immunizations to an infant?

options.A: Deltoid muscle of the upper arm
options.B: Dorsal gluteal muscle of the buttock
options.C: Anterolateral aspect of the thigh
options.D: Anterior abdominal wall near the navel

explanation: The anterolateral thigh muscle is the preferred and safest site for infant intramuscular injections due to muscle mass and nerve safety. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h5)

question: Why must a nurse immediately dispose of used syringes into a safety box?

options.A: To prevent accidental needle-stick injuries and contamination
options.B: To recycle the plastic barrels for future clinical use
options.C: To hide medical waste from visiting health inspectors
options.D: To measure the total number of children immunized daily

explanation: Safety boxes protect healthcare workers and the community from sharps injuries and blood-borne pathogen exposure. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h5)

question: Which tool is primarily used by a mother to track her child's immunization dates?

options.A: Health facility ledger
options.B: Pharmacy prescription pad
options.C: Child health card
options.D: National identity document

explanation: The child health card serves as a personal home-based record tracking specific vaccines received and upcoming appointment dates. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h6)

question: How should a nurse manage a report of a severe adverse event following immunization?

options.A: Investigate and report it promptly through official channels
options.B: Tell the mother to stop bringing other children for vaccines
options.C: Ignore it if the child's fever is below 40 degrees
options.D: Discard all remaining vaccine vials in the facility

explanation: Prompt reporting and investigation of severe AEFIs are mandatory for patient safety and maintaining community trust. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h6)

question: Which factor represents a major barrier to achieving full immunization coverage in Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive availability of solar refrigerators
options.B: Overabundance of functioning cold rooms
options.C: Vaccine hesitancy and misinformation
options.D: Too many trained nurses in rural posts

explanation: Misinformation and vaccine hesitancy prevent many caregivers from accepting immunizations for their children. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h7)

question: What is an effective strategy for reaching children in security-compromised or remote rural areas?

options.A: Relying solely on radio announcements without clinic visits
options.B: Waiting until parents bring children to urban hospitals
options.C: Stopping all immunization activities until peace returns
options.D: Conducting targeted outreach and mobile vaccination sessions

explanation: Outreach and mobile strategies bridge the gap by bringing vaccination services directly to difficult-to-reach populations. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of the cold chain system?

options.A: To speed up the distribution of medical supplies to rural areas
options.B: To manufacture new vaccines locally in primary health care clinics
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing vaccines from suppliers
options.D: To keep vaccines within safe temperature ranges during storage and transport

explanation: The cold chain is strictly designed to maintain specific temperatures to preserve vaccine potency from manufacturer to patient. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T65#GNS214_U1_T65_h1)

question: What happens to a vaccine when its cold chain is broken?

options.A: it only loses effectiveness if exposed to freezing temperatures
options.B: It suffers permanent and irreversible loss of its disease-fighting potency
options.C: It regains potency once placed back inside a functional refrigerator
options.D: It becomes toxic and dangerous to administer to young children

explanation: Vaccine degradation from temperature exposure is absolute and cannot be reversed by cooling it down later. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T65#GNS214_U1_T65_h1)

question: Which cold chain equipment is best suited for transporting vaccines to a remote outreach post?

options.A: A large chest freezer
options.B: A walk-in cold room
options.C: A portable vaccine carrier
options.D: A domestic electric refrigerator

explanation: Vaccine carriers are specifically sized and insulated for short-distance transport and field outreach immunization sessions. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T65#GNS214_U1_T65_h2)

question: Why are different levels of cold chain storage established across the healthcare system?

options.A: To gradually reduce vaccine volumes as they move closer to the end user
options.B: To make vaccine distribution more expensive and bureaucratic
options.C: To ensure every health worker has a personal vaccine refrigerator
options.D: To allow vaccines to adjust to room temperature before administration

explanation: The structure funnels bulk supplies from national stores down to small quantities needed daily at community clinics. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T65#GNS214_U1_T65_h2)

question: What is the standard safe temperature range for storing most routine vaccines in a refrigerator?

options.A: Between plus 2°C and plus 8°C
options.B: Between minus 15°C and minus 20°C
options.C: Between minus 2°C and plus 2°C
options.D: Between plus 15°C and plus 25°C

explanation: The universally accepted cold chain temperature range for routine storage is +2°C to +8°C. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T65#GNS214_U1_T65_h3)

question: What does a Vaccine Vial Monitor (VVM) indicate when its inner square turns darker than the outer circle?

options.A: The vaccine is fresh and safe to administer to infants
options.B: The vaccine needs to be shaken vigorously before drawing up
options.C: The vaccine has been exposed to excessive heat and must be discarded
options.D: The vaccine has been frozen and is now completely useless

explanation: A darkened VVM inner square signals cumulative heat damage, meaning the vaccine's potency is compromised. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T65#GNS214_U1_T65_h3)

question: Where should water packs be placed inside a domestic vaccine refrigerator to help stabilize temperature?

options.A: Outside the refrigerator in room temperature
options.B: Directly on the top shelf next to the freezing compartment
options.C: On the bottom floor of the refrigerator
options.D: Inside the door storage compartments only

explanation: Water packs placed on the floor act as a thermal mass to hold cold temperatures longer during power interruptions. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T65#GNS214_U1_T65_h4)

question: Why is it necessary to condition ice packs before placing them inside an outreach vaccine carrier?

options.A: To allow the vaccines to reach room temperature faster
options.B: To ensure the ice melts completely before reaching the clinic
options.C: To make the vaccine carrier lighter for the nurse to carry
options.D: To prevent the ice packs from freezing and damaging liquid vaccines

explanation: Conditioned ice packs stop the accidental freezing of freeze-sensitive vaccines during transport. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T65#GNS214_U1_T65_h4)

question: What is the primary danger of administering vaccines that have suffered a hidden cold chain breach?

options.A: Patients will develop severe allergic reactions immediately
options.B: Children will receive no real protection against dangerous diseases
options.C: The vaccine vials will explode inside the syringe during injection
options.D: Patients will develop the actual disease the vaccine prevents

explanation: Compromised vaccines fail to generate protective antibodies, leaving the child vulnerable despite being vaccinated. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T65#GNS214_U1_T65_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common cause of a cold chain breach in a clinic?

options.A: Leaving the vaccine refrigerator door open for too long
options.B: Prolonged and unannounced electricity power failures
options.C: Storing vaccines within the safe +2°C to +8°C range
options.D: Using unconditioned frozen ice packs in a vaccine carrier

explanation: Keeping vaccines within the correct temperature range maintains the cold chain rather than breaking it. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T65#GNS214_U1_T65_h5)

question: What should a nurse do first when discovering the facility vaccine refrigerator has stopped working?

options.A: Open the refrigerator door wide to check internal temperature
options.B: Wait until the following morning to see if power returns
options.C: Throw away all the vaccine vials in the safety box
options.D: Transfer threatened vaccines immediately into a cold box with ice packs

explanation: Quickly moving vaccines to a backup cold box prevents further temperature rise and saves the stock. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T65#GNS214_U1_T65_h6)

question: Why is it important to keep a malfunctioning vaccine refrigerator door closed before transferring stock?

options.A: To trap the remaining cold air inside for as long as possible
options.B: To make the room look neat and organized for inspection
options.C: To prevent insects from crawling into the storage unit
options.D: To allow the compressor to repair itself automatically

explanation: Keeping the door closed preserves residual thermal inertia and slows down the warming process. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T65#GNS214_U1_T65_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of the cold chain in immunization?

options.A: To prevent vaccines from losing potency
options.B: To make vaccine distribution easier for staff
options.C: To reduce the manufacturing cost of drugs
options.D: To speed up the vaccine delivery process

explanation: The cold chain protects delicate biological substances from extreme temperature fluctuations that destroy vaccine effectiveness. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h1)

question: Why is the cold chain especially critical in regions like Nigeria?

options.A: High ambient temperatures can rapidly ruin vaccines
options.B: Transport vehicles are always refrigerated naturally
options.C: Patients refuse vaccines stored in standard rooms
options.D: Local health workers lack formal nursing training

explanation: Tropical climates feature high environmental heat, which accelerates vaccine degradation if proper cold storage is absent. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h1)

question: Which equipment is best suited for transporting vaccines to a remote village outreach?

options.A: Domestic deep freezer
options.B: Vaccine carrier
options.C: Walk-in cold room
options.D: Ice-lined refrigerator

explanation: Vaccine carriers are portable, insulated containers built with ice packs specifically for short-distance transport and outreach sessions. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h2)

question: What is the designated safe temperature range for vaccine storage inside an ice-lined refrigerator?

options.A: Between plus 15 and plus 25 degrees Celsius
options.B: Between zero and minus 5 degrees Celsius
options.C: Between plus 2 and plus 8 degrees Celsius
options.D: Between minus 10 and minus 20 degrees Celsius

explanation: Most routine vaccines must be kept refrigerated above freezing and below eight degrees to remain potent and safe. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h2)

question: At what maximum thickness should ice be defrosted inside a vaccine refrigerator?

options.A: Ten centimeters
options.B: Two centimeters
options.C: One inch
options.D: Five millimeters

explanation: Allowing frost to exceed five millimeters reduces the cooling efficiency and threatens the safety of stored vaccines. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h3)

question: Why must a vaccine refrigerator be placed away from the wall?

options.A: To make cleaning the clinic floor much easier
options.B: To comply with fire safety building regulations
options.C: To allow proper air circulation around the compressor
options.D: To prevent patients from tampering with the plug

explanation: Adequate ventilation prevents the cooling motor from overheating and failing prematurely in hot environments. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h3)

question: How often must clinic staff record temperatures of vaccine refrigerators?

options.A: Once a week
options.B: Every hour
options.C: Once a month
options.D: Twice daily

explanation: Morning and evening checks ensure temperature excursions are caught quickly before vaccines spoil completely. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h4)

question: A nurse discovers the vaccine fridge temperature reads plus 12 degrees Celsius. What should she do first?

options.A: Wait until the next morning to see if it drops
options.B: Leave the door open to let cool air enter
options.C: Isolate the vaccines and check the power source
options.D: Throw away all the vaccines immediately

explanation: Isolating the vaccines prevents accidental administration of spoiled doses while investigating the refrigeration fault. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h4)

question: What is the correct way to store vaccine carriers after cleaning?

options.A: Tightly sealed to keep out dust
options.B: Exposed to direct sunlight
options.C: With lids left open to dry
options.D: Stacked directly inside a store room

explanation: Leaving containers open allows complete drying, which prevents fungal growth and unpleasant odors inside the insulation. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h5)

question: Why is ice pack conditioning necessary before packing freeze-sensitive vaccines?

options.A: It removes unwanted bacteria from the ice
options.B: It prevents direct freezing of liquid vaccines
options.C: It increases the freezing time of the box
options.D: It makes the ice packs lighter to carry

explanation: Conditioning ice packs until they sweat ensures they do not drop below zero degrees and ruin vaccines like tetanus toxoid. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h5)

question: What should a nurse check first when a vaccine refrigerator stops working?

options.A: The electrical plug and wall socket connection
options.B: The internal gas pressure of the compressor
options.C: The manufacturing date of the cooling unit
options.D: The thickness of ice lining the evaporator

explanation: Simple power disconnections or loose plugs are the most common and easily fixable causes of equipment stoppage. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a safe action when handling a broken refrigerator?

options.A: Attempting internal electrical wiring repairs alone
options.B: Checking the voltage stabilizer and fuses
options.C: Notifying the designated biomedical technician
options.D: Transferring vaccines to a backup cold box

explanation: Complex electrical repairs require trained technicians to prevent electrocution and further damage to delicate components. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h6)

question: What is the maximum fill level for a needle safety box before disposal?

options.A: One-quarter capacity
options.B: Three-quarters full
options.C: Halfway full of syringes
options.D: Completely packed to the brim

explanation: Stopping at the three-quarter mark prevents needles from protruding and injuring staff handling the waste container. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h7)

question: Why is recapping used injection needles strictly discouraged in clinics?

options.A: It makes the syringe difficult to fit into the safety box
options.B: It greatly increases the risk of accidental needle-stick injuries
options.C: It damages the sharp point of the sterile needle
options.D: It wastes valuable time during mass vaccination campaigns

explanation: Trying to guide a cap back onto a used needle often results in finger punctures and potential bloodborne infections. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h7)

question: What stock management rule dictates that vaccines expiring first should be used first?

options.A: First-Expiry-First-Out
options.B: First-In-First-Stored
options.C: Freezing-Every-First-Order
options.D: Fast-Evaluation-For-Operations

explanation: The FEFO principle minimizes vaccine wastage by ensuring older stock is administered before newly arrived supplies. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h8)

question: What is the primary benefit of maintaining detailed maintenance logbooks for equipment?

options.A: Reducing the cost of purchasing new clinic buildings
options.B: Tracking service history and identifying recurring faults
options.C: Complying with patient confidentiality laws
options.D: Calculating the monthly salaries of health workers

explanation: Detailed records help technicians see patterns in equipment failure, making future repairs quicker and more effective. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h8)

question: What is the primary goal of aseptic techniques during immunization?

options.A: To reduce vaccine manufacturing costs
options.B: To prevent pathogen contamination
options.C: To decrease injection site pain
options.D: To make vaccines work faster

explanation: Aseptic techniques are specifically designed to stop harmful microbes from contaminating sterile items and entering the patient. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h1)

question: Why are injections considered high-risk procedures for infection transmission?

options.A: They are performed too quickly
options.B: They bypass natural skin barriers
options.C: They use expired vaccine vials
options.D: They require expensive equipment

explanation: Breaking the skin destroys the body's first line of defense, allowing any surface microbes on contaminated tools to enter deep tissues directly. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h1)

question: When should an alcohol-based hand rub be used instead of soap and water?

options.A: When hands have visible dirt on them
options.B: Before eating lunch in the ward
options.C: After handling infectious waste
options.D: When hands are not visibly soiled

explanation: Alcohol rubs work quickly to kill germs on clean skin, but physical dirt requires the friction of soap and water to wash away. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h2)

question: A nurse wears clean gloves to vaccinate an infant. Is hand hygiene still necessary?

options.A: Yes, hand hygiene must happen before and after glove use
options.B: Only if the gloves tear during the procedure
options.C: No, gloves completely eliminate the need for hand washing
options.D: Only if the mother requests hand washing

explanation: Gloves can have microscopic holes or become contaminated during removal, making hand hygiene mandatory every single time. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h2)

question: What must always be used to reconstitute a lyophilized vaccine?

options.A: Normal sterile saline from any available brand
options.B: The specific manufacturer-supplied diluent
options.C: Ringer's lactate solution
options.D: Cold sterile water for injection

explanation: Using the exact diluent provided ensures correct chemical balance and prevents contamination or vaccine inactivation. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h3)

question: A nurse notices a vaccine has exceeded its recommended storage temperature range. What is the best action?

options.A: Administer it only to adult clients
options.B: Use the vaccine quickly before it degrades further
options.C: Consult policy guidelines before discarding the affected vials
options.D: Place it back in the freezer to restore potency

explanation: Heat-damaged vaccines lose their potency and fail to protect the client, requiring proper verification and safe disposal. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h3)

question: Why must the alcohol swabbed on a skin site dry completely before injection?

options.A: To ensure the cotton swab sticks better
options.B: To prevent the alcohol from stinging the patient
options.C: To allow the chemical to fully kill surface bacteria
options.D: To make the skin easier to puncture

explanation: Disinfectants need adequate contact time to destroy microbes; injecting through wet alcohol causes burning and reduces antiseptic action. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h4)

question: What happens if an injection site is massaged vigorously after administering certain vaccines?

options.A: It can cause local irritation or rapid drug absorption
options.B: It helps the vaccine spread evenly through the bones
options.C: It stops any potential bleeding instantly
options.D: It speeds up the growth of protective antibodies

explanation: Massaging can alter how the body absorbs the antigen, sometimes increasing local tissue reactions and discomfort. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h4)

question: What practice is strictly forbidden immediately after administering an injection to prevent injury?

options.A: Removing gloves from hands
options.B: Wiping the injection site
options.C: Recording the dose given
options.D: Recapping the used needle

explanation: Trying to recap a used needle with two hands frequently results in accidental stabs to the fingers and hands. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h5)

question: When should a sharps safety box be sealed and replaced?

options.A: After ten needles have been dropped inside
options.B: Only at the end of every calendar month
options.C: When every single side is completely bulging
options.D: When it reaches the specified fill line

explanation: Overfilling a sharps box increases the risk of protruding needles piercing staff during handling or transport. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h5)

question: Which color container is universally used for infectious medical waste like blood-stained cotton?

options.A: Yellow
options.B: Clear
options.C: Black
options.D: Blue

explanation: Yellow bins and bags are standard for infectious and hazardous healthcare waste requiring specialized treatment like incineration. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h6)

question: Why is it dangerous to throw empty glass vaccine vials into ordinary household trash bins?

options.A: It increases the cost of municipal waste trucks
options.B: Government inspectors check household bins daily
options.C: Scavengers or waste sorters could be cut or exposed
options.D: The glass will react chemically with food waste

explanation: Discarding medical items in regular trash exposes members of the community to injury and residual biological hazards. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of sterilization in clinical practice?

options.A: Prevention of rusting on metal tools
options.B: Removal of visible dirt and dust only
options.C: Complete elimination of all microbial life
options.D: Reduction of bacteria to safe levels

explanation: Sterilization destroys every form of microbial life, including resistant spores, unlike disinfection which only reduces pathogen numbers. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h1)

question: Why must instruments be thoroughly washed before entering a sterilizer?

options.A: Soap activates the chemical process inside the machine
options.B: Organic debris protects germs from the sterilizing agent
options.C: Washing prevents the autoclave chamber from rusting
options.D: Dry blood makes metal instruments too heavy to lift

explanation: Residual blood and tissue can shield microorganisms from heat or steam, causing sterilization failure. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h1)

question: What is the standard temperature used for steam sterilization in a basic autoclave?

options.A: 70 degrees Celsius
options.B: 100 degrees Celsius
options.C: 121 degrees Celsius
options.D: 180 degrees Celsius

explanation: The standard temperature of 121°C combined with steam pressure effectively kills bacterial spores. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h2)

question: A nurse notices the autoclave chamber is tightly packed to the top. What is the expected outcome?

options.A: Instruments will achieve double sterility
options.B: Steam will fail to reach all surfaces
options.C: Items will dry out much faster than usual
options.D: The cycle time will automatically shorten

explanation: Overcrowding prevents steam penetration, leaving inner items unsterilized despite running the machine. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h2)

question: Which items are best suited for dry heat sterilization in an oven?

options.A: Disposable syringes and surgical gloves
options.B: Sharp cutting instruments and glassware
options.C: Cloth surgical gowns and linen packs
options.D: Rubber tubing and plastic catheters

explanation: Dry heat does not rust sharp edges or damage dry glassware, making it appropriate for these specific items. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h3)

question: Why is boiling instruments in water for twenty minutes considered disinfection rather than true sterilization?

options.A: Water temperature drops too quickly during the process
options.B: Boiling introduces minerals that coat the metal
options.C: It fails to reliably destroy bacterial endospores
options.D: Microbes develop immediate resistance to hot water

explanation: While boiling kills most vegetative bacteria and viruses, tough endospores survive 100°C temperatures. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h3)

question: Which monitoring method provides the most reliable proof that sterilization was successful?

options.A: Chemical indicator tape on instrument packs
options.B: Visual inspection of dry metal surfaces
options.C: Machine pressure gauge readings
options.D: Biological indicators with bacterial spores

explanation: Biological indicators directly test whether the cycle kills highly resistant test spores, confirming true sterility. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h4)

question: What does a color change on a chemical indicator strip signify?

options.A: Every single microbe inside the pack is dead
options.B: The instrument has been stored long enough
options.C: The pack was exposed to sterilizing conditions
options.D: The machine is completely free of mechanical faults

explanation: Chemical indicators show that heat or steam reached the exterior pack, but they do not guarantee total spore destruction. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h4)

question: What causes strike-through contamination when removing items from an autoclave?

options.A: Opening the door while pressure is zero
options.B: Using chemical indicator tape on paper
options.C: Placing hot packs on a cold wet surface
options.D: Storing dry packs in a wooden cabinet

explanation: Condensation forms when hot packs touch cold surfaces, pulling moisture and airborne microbes through the wrapper. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h5)

question: How is the shelf life of a sterile wrapped instrument pack determined today?

options.A: By a strict limit of exactly seven days from processing
options.B: By the total number of times the autoclave was opened
